raw.query: SELECT d.lead_s, MAX(i.achieved_p99_ms) FILTER (WHERE d.policy = 'reactive') AS reactive_p99_ms, BOOL_AND(i.is_violation) FILTER (WHERE d.policy = 'reactive') AS reactive_violates, MAX(i.achieved_p99_ms) FILTER (WHERE d.policy = 'forecast') AS forecast_p99_ms, BOOL_OR(i.is_violation) FILTER (WHERE d.policy = 'forecast') AS forecast_violates FROM provenance.v_dim AS d JOIN provenance.v_infraction AS i USING (run_id) WHERE d.is_current = TRUE AND d.superseded_by IS NULL AND i.is_current = TRUE AND d.experiment = 'a2' AND d.window_name = 'burst3' AND d.policy IN ('reactive', 'forecast') AND i.sla_metric = 'encoder_delay' AND i.bound_stat = 'p99' GROUP BY d.lead_s ORDER BY d.lead_s;
raw.observed: At leads 15, 30, 45, and 165 s, reactive p99 encoder delays were 9481.285, 16078.706, 28342.19, and 54169.533 ms and violated the SLA at every lead; forecast p99 was 588.37 ms without violation at every lead.
raw.claimed: A one-minute-onset burst defeats an identically informed reactive controller at every lead.
raw.evidence: All four evaluated leads show reactive SLA violations while the paired forecast controller remains below the bound.
